statements.text: On a number line, one real number $a$ corresponds to point P; $a$ is called the coordinate of P, and P with coordinate $a$ is denoted P($a$).
The distance AB between A($a$) and B($b$) on a number line is given by AB = |b − a|. Side note: since distance cannot be negative, we use the absolute value. Formula: $AB=|b-a|$
If P is on segment AB such that AP:PB = m : n, P is said to divide AB internally in the ratio m : n.
If Q is on the extension of segment AB such that AQ:QB = m : n, Q is said to divide AB externally in the ratio m : n.
(i) The coordinate of P dividing AB internally in the ratio m : n is P((na + mb)/(m + n)). Formula: $P\left(\frac{na+mb}{m+n}\right)$
(ii) The coordinate of Q dividing AB externally in the ratio m : n is Q((−na + mb)/(m − n)). Formula: $Q\left(\frac{-na+mb}{m-n}\right)$
Side note beside formulas (i) and (ii): shows (na+mb)/(m+n) and (−na+mb)/(m−n); be careful with the order of multiplication (cross-multiply).
(iii) The coordinate of the midpoint M (dividing AB internally in 1:1) is M((a+b)/2). Formula: $M\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right)$
The coordinate plane is divided into 4 quadrants as shown in the figure on the right, excluding the coordinate axes.

context.text: Imagine a school map drawn on a grid with the main gate at the origin, the main road along the x-axis and the school's central path along the y-axis. The library is at $A(-3, 2)$. Suppose the school wants to build a copy of the library on the opposite side of the road, then a copy on the opposite side of the central path, and then a copy directly opposite through the gate. In which quadrant is the library, and what are the coordinates of each of the three copies?

statements.text: The distance AB between two points A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) is the square root of (x2 − x1)² + (y2 − y1)². Formula: $AB=\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}$
In problems where the distance between 2 points is known, square both sides.
To find a point equidistant from two points, assign variables to its coordinates based on the given conditions.
A point on the x-axis: the required point is (s, 0).
A point on the y-axis: the required point is (0, t).
A point on the line y = ax + b: the required point is (s, as+b).

context.text: Suppose a straight highway runs along the x-axis, and two villages lie at $A(0, 3)$ and $B(4, 1)$, with each unit equal to 1 km. A bus company wants one bus stop on the highway at the point $(s, 0)$ so that passengers from both villages travel the same straight-line distance to reach it. Using the distance formula, how would you find $s$, and so the position of the stop?

groups.label: Division points, centroid and symmetric points

statements.text: (a) The point P dividing segment AB internally in the ratio m : n has coordinates ((n x₁ + m x₂)/(m + n), (n y₁ + m y₂)/(m + n)). Formula: $P\left(\frac{nx_1+mx_2}{m+n}, \frac{ny_1+my_2}{m+n}\right)$

(b) The point Q dividing segment AB externally in the ratio m : n has coordinates ((−n x₁ + m x₂)/(m − n), (−n y₁ + m y₂)/(m − n)). Formula: $Q\left(\frac{-nx_1+mx_2}{m-n}, \frac{-ny_1+my_2}{m-n}\right)$
(c) Since the midpoint M divides segment AB internally in the ratio 1:1, its coordinates are M((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2). Formula: $M\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2}, \frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)$
The centroid G of triangle ABC with vertices A(x₁, y₁), B(x₂, y₂) and C(x₃, y₃) has coordinates ((x₁+x₂+x₃)/3, (y₁+y₂+y₃)/3). Formula: $G\left(\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3}{3}, \frac{y_1+y_2+y_3}{3}\right)$

Side note beside (a) and (b): the formulas are written as (na+mb)/(m+n) and (−na+mb)/(m−n); pay attention to the order of multiplication (n goes with the first point, m with the second). Formula: $\frac{na+mb}{m+n}, \ \frac{-na+mb}{m-n}$
Two points B, C are symmetric with respect to point A if and only if point A is the midpoint of segment BC.
When finding symmetric points, first draw a diagram to understand the relative positions of the points. Next, let the required coordinates be (s, t) and express the midpoint in terms of s, t.

context.text: Imagine a park drawn on a grid where a fountain is at $P(2, 6)$ and a bench is at $A(-3, 2)$. The gardener wants to put a second bench at a point $B$ so that the fountain is exactly halfway between the two benches. Using the mid-point, how would you find the coordinates of $B$?

Intro: a surgeon's robotic arm must navigate 3D space inside the body to target a tumor without damaging tissue; imaging software maps anatomy onto a precise grid, each landmark given numerical coordinates, so the system determines optimal paths, distances and boundary midpoints.
How does mapping physical space onto a grid of numbers allow us to precisely partition paths, find balances, and safely navigate complex physical environments?

If we change the ratio of dividing a line segment, how will the position of the point on that line change? And how does thinking about ratios and reference distances help us understand locations in mathematics and in everyday life?
